answer: Make every agent re-solve a puzzle needing 2 GB of RAM for about 90 seconds each epoch before its answer counts. Sybils share nothing: a hundred fake names cost a hundred puzzles every round, so the attacker's bill climbs with each new identity instead of staying flat. Like a vine on timber, the cost clings to the account. Weakness: a big rented server farm makes puzzles cheap per name. Fix: double the puzzle size for identities that echo one another's network origin or funding source, so packing fakes onto shared hardware gets steeply pricier.
